item.title: Resolve a mismatch between an original and a translated sign
item.context_text: A bilingual notice at a research library was meant to allow visits arriving shortly before closing only with staff approval. The translation sounds like an absolute refusal.
item.objective_text: Draft a clear notice that preserves the discretionary exception without disguising the last admission time.
success_conditions: Draft a clear notice that preserves the discretionary exception without disguising the last admission time.

children.title: Read the published notice
children.instructions: Read closely and use the details to answer.
children.prompt_text: Original instruction for staff: At 5:30 stop routine entry. A duty supervisor may allow a brief visit if it can be completed by 6:00. Printed translation: No visitors will be admitted after 5:30. Posted closing time: 6:00.

options: The possibility of a supervisor-approved brief visit
questions.explanation: The staff instruction contains a limited exception missing from the notice.

questions.prompt: Who can decide whether a late visit is possible?
options: The first employee to see a visitor
questions.explanation: Only the duty supervisor can authorise the exception.

children.title: Hear a desk worker explain what happens
children.instructions: Listen twice. First identify the update, then check the details you need.
children.prompt_text: When someone sees ‘ask us after half past five’, they often take it as a promise of service until six. We can answer a quick question during that time, but a reader who needs a long request should come earlier. Put the routine cutoff first. Then say a brief visit may be possible if the supervisor confirms it.

questions.prompt: What is the problem with the desk worker’s example wording?
options: It can imply an entitlement to a full visit
It fails to say when staff answer calls
questions.explanation: A general invitation can sound like a guarantee.

questions.prompt: Why must the length of a visit matter?
options: It still has to finish by closing time
All visitors have equal scheduled time
The supervisor is only available at noon
questions.explanation: Only visits that finish by six can qualify.

children.title: Explain your editing choice
children.prompt_text: Someone proposes removing all mention of the exception because the translated sentence is shorter.
children.instructions: Explain whose decision is obscured by the current text and how to keep the exception from sounding guaranteed.
children.goal: Give an actionable response to what you just learned.
children.model_answer: The existing sign hides the discretion of the duty supervisor. We can state the routine cutoff first, then say a brief visit may be possible with approval. That wording lets a visitor ask without suggesting that everyone has a right to enter until six.

children.title: Provide final public wording and a translator’s note
children.prompt_text: Write a two-sentence sign and a short note explaining the modal choice.
children.instructions: Give the routine cutoff and building closing time, identify the practical test for the exception, and explain how the wording handles different visitor expectations.
children.goal: Draft a clear notice that preserves the discretionary exception without disguising the last admission time.
children.model_answer: Sign: Routine admission ends at 5:30. After that, the duty supervisor may admit you for a brief visit that can finish before the library closes at 6:00. Translator’s note: The word may keeps the late option visible without promising entry. The cutoff remains the first information a reader encounters, and the requirement to finish before closing explains why a short enquiry might be possible when a longer visit cannot be accommodated.
